title: Marfan Syndrome: Preoperative Cataract Assessment & Surgical Protocol
summary: Marfan Syndrome (MFS) presents unique challenges in cataract surgery, primarily due to zonular instability. This guide covers the essential ocular assessment and risk mitigation strategies required for safe phacoemulsification.

sections.title: Definition & Pathophysiology
sections.content: Marfan Syndrome is an autosomal dominant connective tissue disorder caused by mutations in the FBN1 gene (chromosome 15q21.1) encoding fibrillin-1. In the eye, this results in zonular weakness, leading to ectopia lentis, high myopia, and early-onset cataracts. The lens subluxation is typically superior and temporal.

sections.title: Ocular Examination Findings
content: Slit-lamp: Assess zonular integrity, lens position (iridodonesis, phacodonesis).
Pupillary Dilation: Crucial to view the lens equator and identify missing/stretched zonules.
Refraction: Often high axial myopia or astigmatism due to lens tilt.
Fundoscopy: Screen for peripheral retinal lattice degeneration and retinal detachment risk.

sections.title: Pre-op Assessment Checklist
content: 1. Complete dilated fundus exam (360-degree scleral depression).
2. Axial length measurement (IOL power calculation caution).
3. Keratometry (often shows high astigmatism).
4. Assessment of capsular support (zonular status).
5. Cardiac clearance (MFS associated with aortic root dilation/dissection).

sections.title: Red Flags: Perioperative Emergencies
content: Intraoperative zonular dialysis progression during phaco.
Vitreous prolapse into the anterior chamber (high risk of retinal traction).
Sudden postoperative hypertensive crisis (Aortic dissection risk).
Delayed retinal detachment (up to 15% risk in high myopia).

sections.title: Surgical Toolkit & Strategy
content: Capsular Tension Ring (CTR): Indicated for <180° instability.
Capsular Tension Segments (CTS): Cionni or Ahmed segments for >180° loss.
Trypan Blue: Essential for anterior capsule visualization.
Ophthalmic Viscosurgical Devices (OVD): Use high-viscosity dispersive OVDs.
Femtosecond Laser: Use with caution; docking can cause zonular rupture.

content.explanation: Z-Zonular status check, O-OVD heavy usage, N-No sharp tension, U-Use CTR, L-Look for retinal tears, E-Examine heart (aorta), S-Scleral fixation backup.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Avoid high-vacuum phaco settings; use low flow and slow motion techniques.
Perform a slow, gentle capsulorhexis; ensure it is centered on the lens, not the pupil.
Always discuss the potential for a secondary procedure (e.g., ACIOL or scleral-fixated IOL) with the patient during consent.
In patients with aortic root dilation > 4.5cm, defer elective surgery until cardiac stabilization.
